Apple basic version of iPhone 18 won't launch until early 2027, but it may come with two new Pro series upgrades.

Analyst Jeff Pu says the iPhone 18 will feature 12GB of RAM and a new Dynamic Island design

Apple's annual September event is approaching, with the iPhone 18 Pro and other new products set to debut.

Reports indicate the basic iPhone 18 won't appear at the event. Apple will only unveil the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and the iPhone Ultra.

However, the basic iPhone 18 will still arrive, just delayed until early 2027. It is expected to launch alongside the iPhone 18e and the iPhone Air 2.

According to analyst Jeff Pu, the iPhone 18 may include several Pro-tier upgraded features.

In a recent research note obtained by 9to5Mac, Pu listed his expectations for the basic iPhone 18 based on his sources and supply chain checks. Two features stand out:

  • 12GB of RAM, an upgrade over the 8GB in the iPhone 17
  • A new Dynamic Island design, debuting first on the iPhone 18 Pro

We have previously had conflicting reports about the iPhone 18's RAM. Most recently, Ming-Chi Kuo suggested the device would only feature 9GB of RAM instead of 12GB.

However, Pu's note mentions that the iPhone 18e will have 9GB, while the iPhone 18 will have 12GB. Both models are expected to use the A20 chip.

The smaller Dynamic Island, expected to appear next month, will also be a welcome upgrade.

When Dynamic Island debuted on the iPhone 14 Pro, the basic iPhone 14 still featured a notch. It wasn't until the iPhone 15 that Apple brought Dynamic Island to its lower-tier models.

However, according to Pu's research, Apple may be looking to speed up bringing the new, smaller Dynamic Island design to the basic iPhone.

Are you interested in the basic iPhone 18, or are you planning to get a Pro or Ultra model? Let us know in the comments.
